checklist.step: Extract the flood WYO general ledger data for the close period
actions: In the ERP General Ledger open the flood WYO cost-center/business-unit segment and run the trial balance for the close period.
Export written premium, earned premium, incurred losses, LAE and ceded amounts by state and by policy form.
Tag every line with the NAIC company code and the flood line-of-business code used on the statutory blank.
Hand the extract to the Controller with a checksum total for the tie-out step.
checklist.done: the GL extract is complete by state and line code and the checksum total is recorded.

checklist.step: Build the monthly NFIP Bureau & Statistical Agent output tape
actions: Map the GL extract fields to the current TRRP Plan record layout (policy, claim, and financial transaction record types).
Populate every required TRRP field — transaction type code, policy number, community number, premium and loss amounts — leaving no field blank.
Run the file through the TRRP-format validator before transmission to catch record-length and code-value errors.
Save the validated file as <company-code>-<period>-BSA-tape.dat in the close workpaper folder.
checklist.done: the output tape passes the TRRP format validator with zero record errors.

checklist.step: Reconcile the output tape to the GL flood segment
actions: Sum the tape's premium and loss fields by state and compare to the GL extract totals line by line.
Investigate and clear any variance over $1 by tracing the source transaction in the policy or claims system.
Document each resolved variance with its root cause on the reconciliation workpaper.
Get Controller sign-off on the tie-out before schedule preparation begins.
checklist.done: the tape reconciles to the GL flood segment with every variance cleared and documented.

checklist.step: Prepare the NAIC statutory blank schedules carrying flood business
actions: In the Statutory Reporting (NAIC) tool open the Underwriting & Investment Exhibit, Schedule P and Schedule T for the filing entity.
Populate the flood line-of-business rows from the reconciled GL extract, splitting written/earned premium and incurred losses by state per Schedule T.
Complete Schedule P loss development triangles for the flood line using the reconciled incurred-loss data.
Cross-foot every schedule and resolve any out-of-balance before moving to the next step.
checklist.done: every flood-bearing schedule is populated, cross-foots, and ties to the reconciled GL figures.

checklist.step: Prepare the WYO ULAE/ALAE reimbursement schedule
actions: Pull allocated and unallocated loss adjustment expense for the flood book from the GL extract.
Compute the reimbursable amount per WYO Financial Assistance/Subsidy Arrangement Article III.C expense-allowance formula.
Compare the computed reimbursement to the prior-period allowance and flag any swing over 10% for Controller review.
Attach the schedule to the close workpaper for CFO review.
checklist.done: the ULAE/ALAE reimbursement schedule is computed per Article III.C and any material swing is flagged.

checklist.step: Run the TRRP completeness and validity edit set
actions: Execute the full TRRP edit checklist (required-field, code-value, and cross-record edits) against the built tape.
Log every edit failure with the record identifier and the field that failed.
Correct the source data at the GL or policy-system level, not on the tape directly, and rebuild the tape.
Re-run the edit set until zero failures remain.
checklist.done: the tape passes the full TRRP edit set with zero open failures.

checklist.step: Cross-check flood premium and loss figures to the BSA-issued WYO reports
actions: Retrieve the prior period's BSA-issued Financial Control Plan summary report for the company.
Compare current-period premium and loss totals against the BSA report's running totals for consistency.
Investigate any break exceeding the standard rounding tolerance with the Controller.
Note the comparison result on the close workpaper.
checklist.done: current-period totals are cross-checked to the BSA-issued report and any break is investigated.

checklist.step: Hold the internal tie-out review with the CFO
actions: Present the reconciled GL-to-tape workpaper and the completed statutory schedules to the CFO.
Walk through any flagged variance, the ULAE/ALAE reimbursement figure, and the TRRP edit-clearance evidence.
Record meeting decisions and any required schedule corrections.
Confirm the close package is ready for certification.
checklist.done: the CFO tie-out meeting is held and every open item from it is closed before certification.

checklist.step: Obtain CFO certification of the statutory statement
actions: Review the final statutory blank package and the reconciled BSA output tape.
Sign the statutory certification page confirming the statements fairly present the company's financial condition.
Date and file the signed certification with the close workpaper.
Authorize the Regulatory Reporting Analyst to proceed to filing.
checklist.done: the CFO's dated certification is attached to the close package before any filing is submitted.

checklist.step: File the statutory statement
actions: In the Statutory Reporting (NAIC) tool select the filing entity and the correct filing period (Quarterly or Annual).
Upload the certified schedules and run the NAIC electronic filing validation before submission.
Submit the filing and capture the NAIC submission confirmation number.
File the confirmation in the close workpaper folder.
checklist.done: the statement is filed with a captured NAIC confirmation number before the due date.

checklist.step: Transmit the monthly BSA output tape
actions: Transmit the validated, zero-error tape to the NFIP Bureau & Statistical Agent through the designated WYO transmission channel.
Record the transmission date and batch confirmation number.
Notify the CFO if the transmission window is within 2 business days of the WYO Financial Control Plan cutoff.
File the transmission log with the close workpaper.
checklist.done: the monthly tape is transmitted and a batch confirmation number is on file.

checklist.step: Confirm BSA acceptance of the tape
actions: Retrieve the BSA acknowledgment report for the submitted batch.
Confirm the report shows zero rejected records.
Where rejects exist, open a correction cycle and resubmit within the WYO-allowed resubmission window.
File the clean acknowledgment report with the close workpaper.
checklist.done: a zero-reject BSA acknowledgment is on file for the period, or rejects are corrected and resubmitted within the window.

checklist.step: Log and remediate any rejects or restatements
actions: Open a tracker issue for every BSA reject or statutory restatement with the affected period and schedule.
Assign a root cause and an owner for the correction.
Set a remediation date and route material restatements to the CFO for sign-off.
Close the issue only once the corrected filing or tape is accepted.
checklist.done: every reject or restatement has a logged root cause, owner, remediation date and confirmed correction.

checklist.step: Archive the filed statement and confirmations
actions: Move the certified schedules, NAIC confirmation number, and BSA acknowledgment into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label to the close package.
Confirm the record is indexed and searchable by period and company code.
checklist.done: the close package is archived, labelled for 7-year retention, and retrievable by period.

checklist.step: Update the close and filing calendar for the next period
actions: Roll the NAIC quarterly/annual due dates and the monthly BSA tape cutoff forward to the next period.
Confirm the T-10/T-5/T-1 reminder alerts are set against the new dates.
Flag any change to the TRRP layout or NAIC blank instructions for the next close cycle.
checklist.done: the next period's due dates and reminders are loaded onto the filing calendar.

testing.step: Build the population of statutory filings and BSA tape submissions
actions: Extract from the Statutory Reporting (NAIC) tool every quarterly and annual filing submitted for the flood WYO entity in the test period.
Extract every monthly BSA tape transmission log for the same period.
Reconcile the filing count to the close calendar to confirm none are missing from the population.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the close calendar and signed as complete.

testing.step: Independently reconcile the GL to each filed statement
actions: Pull the GL flood-segment trial balance for the period directly from the ERP, independent of the close workpaper.
Compare GL totals to the filed schedule totals line by line.
List any unexplained variance over $1 as an exception.
testing.done: every filed statement is independently reconciled to the GL with variances listed as exceptions or cleared.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of annual statement filings in the test period.
Take a random, seeded sample of quarterly filings and monthly BSA tapes, minimum 8 items.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every annual filing.

testing.step: Re-perform the schedule build for the sample
actions: For each sampled filing, independently rebuild the Schedule T and Schedule P flood rows from the reconciled GL extract.
Compare the re-performed figures to the filed schedule figures.
Log any difference, including differences that net to zero across states.
testing.done: each sampled schedule has an independent re-performance note with any difference logged.

testing.step: Trace the BSA tape acknowledgment for the sample
actions: Retrieve the BSA acknowledgment report for each sampled monthly tape.
Confirm the report shows zero rejected records for the sampled batch.
Where rejects existed, confirm the correction cycle closed before the next month's tape was due.
testing.done: every sampled tape traces to a zero-reject acknowledgment or a closed correction cycle.

testing.step: Recompute the ULAE/ALAE reimbursement figure for the sample
actions: Recompute the Article III.C expense-allowance reimbursement for each sampled period from the GL extract.
Compare to the amount filed and flag any variance exceeding 2%.
Confirm any prior flagged swing over 10% received Controller review evidence.
testing.done: the reimbursement figure is recomputed for the sample and variances over 2% are logged.

testing.step: Recompute the filing-deadline maths
actions: For each sampled filing, compute the due date (quarter end + 45 days, or March 1 for annual) and compare to the actual NAIC confirmation timestamp.
For each sampled tape, compare the transmission date to the WYO Financial Control Plan cutoff.
Log any late filing or transmission as an exception regardless of whether it was later accepted.
testing.done: every sampled filing and tape is confirmed on-time or logged as a late exception.

testing.step: Verify the CFO certification predates the filing
actions: Pull the signed CFO certification page for each sampled annual and quarterly filing.
Confirm the certification date is on or before the NAIC submission timestamp.
Flag any filing submitted without a dated certification on file.
testing.done: every sampled filing has a dated CFO certification predating its submission, or is flagged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception identified in the test with the period, schedule and impact.
Assign a root cause and an owner for correction.
Set a remediation date and carry open items into the next quarter's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-unreconciled-break threshold.
Write the test conclusion with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper and report results to the CFO.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported to the CFO.

checklist.step: Build the filing distribution list for the period
actions: Pull the current list of writing states for the flood WYO book from the policy administration system.
For each state, confirm whether a direct state filing is required in addition to the NAIC filing, and note the state DOI portal.
Load the resulting distribution list into the filing calendar for the period.
checklist.done: the distribution list names every state requiring a filing and its submission channel.

checklist.step: Confirm the certified statutory package is filing-ready
actions: Confirm the CFO-certified schedules from the statutory close are loaded in the Statutory Reporting (NAIC) tool.
Verify the filing period, company code and blank version match the current NAIC requirements.
Flag any missing schedule to the Controller before proceeding.
checklist.done: the certified package in the filing tool matches the required blank version with no missing schedule.

checklist.step: Submit the NAIC filing
actions: In the Statutory Reporting (NAIC) tool select Submit Filing for the period and run the electronic validation check.
Correct any validation error and resubmit until the file passes.
Capture the NAIC confirmation number and timestamp.
Log the confirmation on the filing tracker.
checklist.done: the NAIC filing is submitted, validated, and its confirmation number is logged.

checklist.step: Submit each required state supplemental filing
actions: For each state requiring a direct filing, log in to the state DOI portal and locate the flood/WYO supplemental filing form.
Upload the state-specific schedule and any required transmittal letter.
Submit and capture the state's confirmation number or receipt.
Log each state confirmation on the filing tracker.
checklist.done: every required state filing is submitted with a captured confirmation on the tracker.

checklist.step: Reconcile submitted filings against the distribution list
actions: Compare the filing tracker's confirmed submissions against the full distribution list for the period.
Identify any state or the NAIC filing still outstanding.
Escalate any outstanding item within 2 business days of its due date to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: every item on the distribution list shows a confirmed submission or a logged escalation.

checklist.step: Verify filing timeliness against the due-date calendar
actions: Compare each confirmation timestamp to the due date recorded on the filing calendar.
Flag any submission within 1 business day of its deadline for a process-improvement note.
Record the on-time result for each filing on the tracker.
checklist.done: every filing's timeliness against its due date is recorded on the tracker.

checklist.step: Handle any rejected or bounced state submission
actions: Where a state portal rejects the filing, read the rejection reason and correct the underlying schedule or transmittal.
Resubmit within the state's allowed resubmission window.
Notify the Regulatory Reporting Manager of any rejection that risks the due date.
checklist.done: every rejected submission is corrected and resubmitted within the state's window.

checklist.step: Request an extension where a deadline cannot be met
actions: Where the close package will not be ready in time, contact the affected state DOI's financial filing unit to request a formal extension.
Get the extension approval in writing and log it on the filing tracker.
Notify the Head of Compliance of the extension and the revised due date.
checklist.done: any deadline at risk has either a met due date or a documented, approved extension.

checklist.step: Log any missed deadline as an exception
actions: Open a tracker issue for any filing submitted after its due date without an approved extension.
Record root cause, the state affected, and the corrective action.
Route the issue to the Head of Compliance for sign-off.
checklist.done: every missed deadline has a logged root cause and Head of Compliance sign-off.

checklist.step: Get Head of Compliance sign-off on the period's filing status
actions: Review the completed filing tracker for the period, including any exceptions or extensions.
Sign off confirming all filings are either submitted on time, submitted under an approved extension, or logged as an exception with remediation.
File the signed status summary with the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: the Head of Compliance has signed off on the complete filing status for the period.

checklist.step: Archive filing confirmations and correspondence
actions: Move every NAIC and state confirmation, plus extension correspondence, into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm records are indexed by state and filing period.
checklist.done: all filing confirmations are archived, retention-labelled, and retrievable by state and period.

checklist.step: Notify downstream teams of any state-specific filing findings
actions: Where a state rejection revealed a data quality issue, notify the Controller and the policy administration data owner.
Track the underlying data fix to close in the issue tracker.
Confirm the fix is reflected before the next filing cycle.
checklist.done: any data-quality root cause behind a rejection is tracked to a confirmed fix before the next cycle.

checklist.step: Update the state distribution list for regulatory changes
actions: Monitor NAIC and state DOI bulletins for changes to filing requirements or due dates affecting flood WYO business.
Update the distribution list and filing calendar for any change.
Notify the Regulatory Reporting Manager of material changes.
checklist.done: the distribution list and calendar reflect the current NAIC/state requirements at all times.

checklist.step: Confirm filing fee payments accompany each submission
actions: Identify any state that requires a filing fee alongside the statutory submission.
Confirm payment (EFT or check) was submitted with the filing and capture the payment confirmation.
Log the payment confirmation next to the filing confirmation on the tracker.
checklist.done: every fee-requiring state filing has a matched payment confirmation on the tracker.

checklist.step: Roll the filing calendar forward to the next period
actions: Set the next period's NAIC and state due dates on the filing calendar.
Confirm T-15/T-5/T-1 reminders are configured against the new dates.
Close out the current period's tracker entries.
checklist.done: the next period's due dates and reminders are loaded and the current period tracker is closed.

testing.step: Build the population of required filings for the period
actions: Independently derive the required filing list from the current NAIC schedule and each writing state's DOI requirements.
Compare to the distribution list used by Regulatory Reporting to confirm completeness.
List any state missing from the working distribution list as an exception.
testing.done: the independently derived population matches the working distribution list or gaps are logged.

testing.step: Reconcile the filing tracker to actual submissions
actions: In the Statutory Reporting (NAIC) tool pull the actual submission history for the period.
Compare submission dates and confirmation numbers to the filing tracker.
List any tracker entry without a matching system submission as an exception.
testing.done: every tracker entry is matched to an actual system submission or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of state filings that were flagged late or extended.
Take a random, seeded sample of the remaining on-time filings, minimum 10 items.
Record the seed, population size and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every late or extended filing.

testing.step: Trace each sampled filing to its regulator confirmation
actions: For each sampled filing, open the state DOI portal or NAIC tool and locate the corresponding submission record.
Confirm the submission date, entity, and period match the tracker.
Capture a screenshot of the confirmation into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled filing traces to a real regulator confirmation matching the tracker.

testing.step: Recompute the due date and lateness for each sampled filing
actions: Independently compute the due date from the NAIC schedule or the state's filing rule.
Compare to the actual confirmation timestamp.
Flag any filing submitted after the recomputed due date without a matching approved extension.
testing.done: every sampled filing's timeliness is independently recomputed and any breach is flagged.

testing.step: Verify any extension claimed in the sample
actions: For each sampled filing citing an extension, locate the written approval from the state DOI.
Confirm the extended due date covers the actual submission date.
Treat an extension without written approval as a late-filing exception, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every claimed extension in the sample is backed by a written, dated approval covering the submission.

testing.step: Verify fee payment for fee-requiring states in the sample
actions: For each sampled state requiring a filing fee, locate the payment confirmation.
Confirm the payment date is on or before the filing due date.
Log any missing or late payment as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled fee-requiring filing has a verified, timely payment or a logged exception.

testing.step: Test the Head of Compliance sign-off evidence
actions: Confirm a dated Head of Compliance sign-off exists for the period covering all filings, extensions and exceptions.
Confirm the sign-off date is after the last filing in the period.
Flag any period missing a sign-off.
testing.done: each tested period has a dated, complete Head of Compliance sign-off.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception found in the test with the state, filing and impact.
Assign a root cause and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open items into next quarter's test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date.

Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper and report results to the Head of Compliance.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and late-filing rate is filed and reported.

Log the confirmation on the filing tracker.

checklist.done: any CoA gap has an initiated application and a go-live date no earlier than the expected grant.

checklist.step: Confirm the current-year WYO Financial Assistance/Subsidy Arrangement is executed
actions: Retrieve the company's most recently executed WYO Financial Assistance/Subsidy Arrangement.
Confirm it matches the exact form and substance published in the Federal Register for the current fiscal year, with no modification.
Confirm it was executed at least 6 months before its effective date.
Flag any deviation from the published form to General Counsel.
checklist.done: the current-year WYO Arrangement is confirmed executed, unmodified, and timely relative to its effective date.

checklist.step: Verify no gap exists between the CoA and the WYO Arrangement's state coverage
actions: Compare the list of states covered by the WYO Arrangement to the states covered by an active CoA.
List any state present in one but not the other.
Route any mismatch to General Counsel for resolution before market entry.
checklist.done: the WYO Arrangement and CoA state lists are reconciled with any mismatch routed for resolution.

checklist.step: Get General Counsel sign-off on the market-entry licensing gate
actions: Review the CoA and WYO Arrangement verification evidence in the market-entry file.
Sign the market-entry gate approval confirming both preconditions are met.
Return the signed approval to the Regulatory Affairs Manager.
checklist.done: General Counsel's signed gate approval is on file before underwriting is released to write business.

checklist.step: Release the market-entry gate to underwriting
actions: Notify the Insurance Product Manager and underwriting that the state/line is cleared to bind.
Record the gate-release date on the market-entry file.
Confirm the policy administration system's state-availability configuration matches the cleared date.
checklist.done: underwriting is notified and the policy administration system reflects the same cleared date.

checklist.step: Monitor CoA status continuously for active states
actions: Run a monthly sweep of the internal regulatory license-tracking system for any CoA nearing renewal or flagged for suspension.
Cross-check any flagged state against the state DOI lookup.
Escalate any CoA at risk of lapse to General Counsel at 90 days before expiration.
checklist.done: a monthly CoA sweep is performed and at-risk states are escalated at 90 days out.

checklist.step: Suspend new business in any state where the CoA lapses
actions: On notice of a CoA lapse, immediately instruct underwriting to stop binding new flood business in that state.
Confirm the policy administration system's state-availability flag is turned off the same day.
Track the renewal or reinstatement to completion before re-enabling the state.
checklist.done: new business is stopped the same day as any CoA lapse and only resumes on confirmed reinstatement.

checklist.step: Log any gap as a compliance breach
actions: Open a tracker issue for any period business was bound without a current CoA or WYO Arrangement.
Assign root cause, states affected, and policy count impacted.
Route to General Counsel for a self-report assessment.
checklist.done: every gap period is logged with root cause, states, policy count, and routed for self-report assessment.

checklist.step: Self-report a licensing breach where required
actions: Assess whether the breach requires self-report to the state DOI or FEMA/the NFIP Bureau.
Prepare and submit the self-report with the remediation plan.
File the submission confirmation with the market-entry record.
checklist.done: any required self-report is submitted with a remediation plan and its confirmation filed.

checklist.step: Retain CoA and WYO Arrangement evidence
actions: Move the CoA screenshots, the executed WYO Arrangement, and the gate approval into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply retention for the life of the state authority plus 7 years.
Confirm the record is indexed by state and effective date.
checklist.done: CoA and Arrangement evidence is archived, retention-labelled, and retrievable by state.

checklist.step: Update the CoA renewal calendar
actions: Load each state's CoA renewal date onto the licensing calendar.
Set 90/60/30-day reminders ahead of each renewal.
Confirm the calendar matches the internal regulatory system's current CoA status.
checklist.done: the CoA renewal calendar is current and reminders are set for every active state.

checklist.step: Track the next WYO Arrangement re-subscription
actions: Monitor the Federal Register for publication of the next fiscal year's WYO Financial Assistance/Subsidy Arrangement.
Set the 9/6/3-month reminders against its stated effective date.
Route the new form to General Counsel for execution well ahead of the 6-month precondition.
checklist.done: the next fiscal year's WYO Arrangement is tracked and routed for execution ahead of the 6-month deadline.

checklist.step: Brief underwriting on any upcoming state-availability change
actions: Notify underwriting leadership ahead of any planned CoA suspension, renewal gap, or new-state clearance.
Confirm underwriting's system configuration change is scheduled to match the compliance date.
Record the briefing and acknowledgment.
checklist.done: underwriting is briefed and acknowledges every upcoming state-availability change ahead of its effective date.

testing.step: Build the population of states with flood WYO business bound in the test period
actions: Extract the list of states with new or renewed flood WYO business from the policy administration system.
Pull the corresponding CoA status for each state from the internal regulatory license-tracking system.
Reconcile the two lists and flag any state with business but no matching CoA record.
testing.done: the bound-business population is reconciled to CoA records with gaps flagged.

testing.step: Independently verify CoA status against the state DOI
actions: For each state in the population, independently look up the company's license status on the state DOI's public lookup.
Compare to the internal system's recorded status.
Log any mismatch or lapsed CoA as an exception.
testing.done: every state's CoA status is independently confirmed against the state DOI or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of states newly entered in the test period.
Take a random, seeded sample of renewal states, minimum 10 items.
Record the seed, population size and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every new-entry state.

testing.step: Verify the WYO Arrangement covering the sample
actions: Pull the executed WYO Arrangement in effect for each sampled state's bind date.
Compare it against the Federal Register published form for that fiscal year to confirm it is unmodified.
Confirm it was executed at least 6 months before its effective date.
Log any discrepancy as an exception.
testing.done: the WYO Arrangement's currency and form are independently verified for the sample.

testing.step: Trace the market-entry gate approval for the sample
actions: Locate the General Counsel sign-off for each sampled state's market entry.
Confirm the sign-off date precedes the first bound policy's effective date.
Log any state with business bound before the gate sign-off as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled state's gate approval is confirmed to predate the first bound policy, or logged.

testing.step: Recompute the timing gap between CoA grant and first bound policy
actions: For each sampled state, compute the days between the CoA active/grant date and the first bound policy's effective date.
Confirm the first bound policy date is on or after the CoA active date.
Log any policy bound before CoA activation as a compliance breach exception, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: the CoA-to-bind timing is recomputed for every sampled state with any pre-activation bind logged as a breach.

testing.step: Verify the monthly CoA sweep evidence
actions: Confirm a documented monthly CoA sweep exists for each month in the test period.
Confirm any flagged at-risk CoA in the sweep was escalated at the 90-day mark.
Log any missing sweep or missed escalation as an exception.
testing.done: monthly sweep documentation and 90-day escalations are confirmed for the test period, or gaps are logged.

testing.step: Verify any logged breach received a self-report assessment
actions: Pull every tracker issue logged as a CoA or WYO Arrangement gap in the test period.
Confirm each has a documented General Counsel self-report assessment.
Log any breach without an assessment as an exception.
testing.done: every logged breach has a confirmed self-report assessment or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception found in the test.
Assign a root cause and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open items into the next annual test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the breach rate against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper and report results to General Counsel.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and breach rate is filed and reported to General Counsel.

checklist.step: Verify the producer's license and line of authority before solicitation
actions: In NIPR, run a license lookup for the producer's NPN in the state where the flood policy will be solicited.
Confirm the license is Active and lists the Property or Flood line of authority.
Cross-check the result against the state DOI's producer lookup for the same status.
Record the verification result and timestamp against the solicitation record.
checklist.done: an Active license with the correct line of authority is confirmed in both NIPR and the state DOI lookup before solicitation.

checklist.step: Block solicitation for any producer failing verification
actions: Where NIPR shows no active license or the wrong line of authority, place a solicitation hold in the agency/producer management system.
Notify the producer's agency principal and the Broker Relationship Manager of the hold and its reason.
Release the hold only on confirmed, re-verified license correction.
checklist.done: no solicitation hold is released without a re-verified, corrected NIPR license status.

checklist.step: Verify community participation before the policy can bind
actions: Look up the property's community in the FEMA Community Status Book / Community Information System.
Confirm the community is Participating and not Suspended or on Probation.
Attach the community-status confirmation to the policy file.
Reject binding if the community is non-participating or suspended.
checklist.done: a Participating, non-suspended community status is confirmed and attached to the policy file before bind.

checklist.step: Verify producer appointment status before appointment is processed
actions: In NIPR, submit or confirm the appointment transaction for the producer in the target state.
Verify the state's appointment fee is paid and the transaction is accepted, not pending.
Record the appointment effective date in the agency/producer management system.
checklist.done: the appointment transaction is accepted in NIPR with a recorded effective date before the producer is enabled to bind.

checklist.step: Enable the producer to bind flood business only after both checks pass
actions: Confirm both the license/line-of-authority check and the appointment check are recorded as passed.
Enable the producer's binding authority for flood in the agency/producer management system.
Log the enablement date and both supporting verification references.
checklist.done: binding authority is enabled only with both verification checks passed and logged.

checklist.step: Run the daily NIPR license-status feed and act on lapses
actions: Load the daily NIPR license-status feed for all appointed flood producers.
Identify any producer whose license lapsed, was suspended, or was revoked overnight.
Same-day, suspend the producer's binding authority in the agency/producer management system.
Notify the Producer Compliance Manager of every same-day suspension.
checklist.done: every overnight license lapse is actioned with a same-day binding suspension and notification.

checklist.step: Investigate any policy bound during a license lapse window
actions: Query the policy administration system for any flood policy bound by the lapsed producer between the lapse date and the suspension date.
List every affected policy with its bind date and premium.
Route the list to the Producer Compliance Manager for disposition.
checklist.done: every policy bound during a lapse window is identified and routed for disposition.

checklist.step: Disposition unlicensed-solicitation exposures
actions: Determine whether affected policies must be rewritten through a licensed producer, cancelled and rewritten, or handled via a state-specific cure provision.
Determine whether commission paid to the unlicensed producer must be recovered.
Document the disposition decision for each affected policy.
checklist.done: every affected policy has a documented disposition decision including any commission recovery.

checklist.step: Reconcile appointment records against the NIPR system of record monthly
actions: Export the appointed-producer list from the agency/producer management system.
Compare it to the NIPR appointment history for each producer.
List any mismatch (appointed internally but not in NIPR, or vice versa) for correction.
checklist.done: internal appointment records are reconciled to NIPR monthly with mismatches corrected.

checklist.step: Log every unlicensed or unappointed solicitation as an exception
actions: Open a tracker issue for each confirmed unlicensed-solicitation or unappointed-bind incident.
Assign root cause (feed delay, missed verification, agency error) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and track to closure.
checklist.done: every incident has a logged root cause, owner, and remediation date tracked to closure.

checklist.step: Assess self-report obligations for confirmed unlicensed sales
actions: Review confirmed unlicensed-solicitation incidents for state self-report thresholds.
Prepare and submit any required self-report with the remediation plan.
File the submission confirmation with the incident record.
checklist.done: any required self-report for a confirmed unlicensed sale is submitted and its confirmation filed.

checklist.step: Retain verification and appointment evidence
actions: Move NIPR verification logs, community-status confirmations, and appointment records into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the record is indexed by producer NPN and state.
checklist.done: verification and appointment evidence is archived, retention-labelled, and retrievable by producer.

checklist.step: Brief agency principals on verification requirements
actions: Communicate the pre-solicitation and pre-appointment verification requirements to every agency principal writing flood business.
Confirm agency onboarding materials reflect the current NIPR-based process.
Record acknowledgment from each agency principal.
checklist.done: every agency principal has acknowledged the current verification requirements.

checklist.step: Review community-status refresh cadence
actions: Re-check community participation status at each policy renewal, not only at new business.
Flag any community that moved to Suspended or Probation status since the prior term.
Route flagged renewals to underwriting for a non-renewal or coverage-restriction decision.
checklist.done: community status is re-checked at every renewal with status changes routed for a coverage decision.

checklist.step: Report the period's licensing metrics to the Producer Compliance Manager
actions: Summarize verification volume, lapses actioned, and open exceptions for the period.
Present the summary to the Producer Compliance Manager.
Incorporate any process improvement into next period's procedure.
checklist.done: the period's licensing metrics are reported and any process improvement is incorporated.

testing.step: Build the population of flood policies bound in the test period
actions: Extract every flood WYO policy bound in the test period from the policy administration system, with the writing producer's NPN.
Reconcile the extract count to the underwriting bind report for completeness.
testing.done: the bound-policy population is reconciled to the bind report and signed as complete.

testing.step: Independently verify producer license status at the bind date
actions: For each policy in the population, look up the producer's NIPR license history as of the bind date.
Confirm the license was Active with the correct line of authority on that date.
List any policy bound while the license was lapsed, suspended, or lacking the line of authority as an exception.
testing.done: producer license status at bind is independently verified for the full population with exceptions listed.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of policies flagged as exceptions in the population check.
Take a random, seeded sample of the remaining clean population, minimum 25 items.
Record the seed, population size and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every flagged exception.

testing.step: Verify appointment status for the sample
actions: For each sampled policy, confirm the producer's appointment was Active in NIPR at the bind date.
Compare to the appointment effective date recorded in the agency/producer management system.
Log any mismatch or unappointed bind as an exception.
testing.done: appointment status at bind is independently verified for the sample with mismatches logged.

testing.step: Verify community participation status for the sample
actions: For each sampled policy, check the property's community status in the FEMA Community Status Book as of the bind date.
Confirm the community was Participating and not Suspended.
Log any policy bound in a non-participating or suspended community as an exception.
testing.done: community participation status at bind is verified for the sample with exceptions logged.

testing.step: Re-perform the daily lapse-feed reconciliation for a sample period
actions: Select 5 dates within the test period and independently pull the NIPR license-status feed for those dates.
Compare to the internal suspension log to confirm every lapse was actioned same day.
Log any lapse not actioned same day as an exception.
testing.done: the lapse-feed reconciliation is re-performed for the sample dates with same-day action confirmed or logged.

testing.step: Trace disposition of confirmed exceptions
actions: For each confirmed unlicensed or unappointed exception, locate the Producer Compliance Manager's disposition decision.
Confirm any required commission recovery or policy rewrite was completed.
Log any exception without a completed disposition.
testing.done: every confirmed exception's disposition is traced to completion or logged as open.

testing.step: Verify self-report submissions for material breaches
actions: For any exception exceeding the state's self-report threshold, confirm a General Counsel self-report submission exists.
Confirm the submission includes the remediation plan.
Log any missing required self-report.
testing.done: self-report submissions are confirmed for every threshold-exceeding exception or logged as missing.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception found in the test.
Assign a root cause and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open items into next month's test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper and report results to the Producer Compliance Manager.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Intake the appointment or termination event
actions: Receive the event trigger — new agency contract, producer offboarding, or a for-cause termination decision — from the Broker Relationship Manager or HR.
Open a case in the agency/producer management system recording the event type, producer NPN, and event date.
Identify the state's statutory processing window for this event type from the licensing-rule reference.
checklist.done: a case is opened with event type, producer NPN, event date, and the applicable statutory window identified.

checklist.step: Submit the appointment transaction in NIPR
actions: In NIPR, run Appointment Processing for the producer's NPN in the target state.
Confirm the producer's underlying license and line of authority are Active before submitting.
Submit the appointment transaction and pay the state's appointment fee where required.
Capture the NIPR transaction confirmation number and date.
checklist.done: the appointment transaction is submitted in NIPR with a captured confirmation number and date.

checklist.step: Submit the termination transaction in NIPR
actions: In NIPR, run Termination Processing for the producer's NPN in the affected state.
Select the correct termination reason code (voluntary, for-cause, non-renewal).
Submit the transaction and capture the confirmation number and date.
Update the agency/producer management system to reflect the termination effective date.
checklist.done: the termination transaction is submitted in NIPR with the correct reason code, confirmation number, and date.

checklist.step: Confirm processing lands inside the statutory window
actions: Compute the days elapsed between the event date and the NIPR transaction confirmation date.
Compare to the state's statutory window (commonly 15-30 days).
Flag any case approaching the window's midpoint for expedited processing.
checklist.done: every case's processing time is computed against the statutory window and at-risk cases are expedited.

checklist.step: Prepare and send the state-required termination notice
actions: Identify whether the state requires a separate written notice to the producer and/or the DOI beyond the NIPR transaction.
Draft the notice using the state's required content (reason, effective date, appeal rights where applicable).
Send the notice within the state's specific notice period and retain proof of delivery.
checklist.done: any state-required termination notice is sent within its notice period with delivery proof retained.

checklist.step: Prepare the for-cause termination regulatory report
actions: For a for-cause termination, compile the underlying facts, dates, and any consumer harm identified.
Complete the state's for-cause termination report form where the state requires one.
Route the draft to General Counsel for review before submission.
checklist.done: the for-cause report is compiled with supporting facts and routed for General Counsel review.

checklist.step: Get General Counsel review before submitting a for-cause report
actions: Review the for-cause report for legal sufficiency and consistency with any related investigation file.
Approve or revise the report language.
Clear the report for submission to the state DOI.
checklist.done: General Counsel has cleared the for-cause report before it is submitted.

checklist.step: Submit the for-cause report and capture confirmation
actions: Submit the cleared for-cause report to the state DOI within its required window.
Capture the submission confirmation.
Log the confirmation on the case record.
checklist.done: the for-cause report is submitted within the state's window with a captured confirmation.

checklist.step: Verify binding authority is revoked on termination effective date
actions: Confirm the terminated producer's binding authority is disabled in the policy administration system as of the termination effective date.
Check for any policy bound after the effective date by the terminated producer.
Escalate any post-termination bind to the Producer Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: binding authority is confirmed disabled on the effective date with any post-termination bind escalated.

checklist.step: Handle any appointment or termination processed outside the window
actions: Open a tracker issue for any case where the NIPR confirmation date fell outside the statutory window.
Assign root cause (intake delay, NIPR rejection, fee issue) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where the delay created a coverage or compliance exposure, notify the Producer Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: every out-of-window case has a logged root cause, owner, remediation date, and exposure notification where applicable.

checklist.step: Assess exposure from any late-processed case
actions: Determine whether any policy was solicited or bound during the late-processing window without proper appointment.
Apply the disposition process for any unappointed-bind exposure identified.
Document the exposure assessment and its outcome.
checklist.done: every late-processed case has a documented exposure assessment and disposition outcome.

checklist.step: Retain appointment and termination records
actions: Move the NIPR confirmations, termination notices, and any for-cause report into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the record is indexed by producer NPN and event date.
checklist.done: appointment and termination records are archived, retention-labelled, and retrievable by producer.

checklist.step: Reconcile the case log to NIPR monthly
actions: Export the month's appointment/termination case log from the agency/producer management system.
Compare each case to its NIPR transaction history for a matching confirmation.
Correct any case with a missing or mismatched NIPR record.
checklist.done: every case in the month's log is reconciled to a matching NIPR transaction record.

checklist.step: Report processing-window performance to the Producer Compliance Manager
actions: Summarize the month's average processing time, on-time rate, and any out-of-window cases.
Present the summary to the Producer Compliance Manager.
Identify any state trending toward window breaches for process attention.
checklist.done: monthly processing-window performance is reported with any trending state flagged.

checklist.step: Update the statutory-window reference for regulatory changes
actions: Monitor state DOI bulletins for changes to appointment/termination processing windows.
Update the licensing-rule reference used in case intake.
Communicate any window change to the licensing team before the next case is affected.
checklist.done: the statutory-window reference is current and any change is communicated before it affects a case.

testing.step: Build the population of appointment and termination events
actions: Extract every appointment and termination case from the agency/producer management system for the test period.
Reconcile the count to HR/agency offboarding records and new-agency-contract records for completeness.
testing.done: the event population is reconciled to source records and signed as complete.

testing.step: Independently verify NIPR transaction confirmation dates
actions: For each event in the population, pull the NIPR transaction history and confirm the transaction date and type.
Compare the confirmation date to the case log's recorded date.
List any mismatch or missing NIPR transaction as an exception.
testing.done: NIPR transaction confirmation is independently verified for the full population with mismatches listed.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of for-cause terminations in the test period.
Take a random, seeded sample of remaining appointments/terminations, minimum 25 items.
Record the seed, population size and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every for-cause termination.

testing.step: Recompute the statutory-window compliance for the sample
actions: For each sampled case, independently compute days elapsed from event date to NIPR confirmation date.
Compare against the state's statutory window applicable at the event date.
Log any case exceeding the window as an exception.
testing.done: statutory-window compliance is recomputed for the sample with breaches logged.

testing.step: Verify termination notice delivery for the sample
actions: For each sampled termination requiring a state-specific notice, locate the delivery proof.
Confirm delivery occurred within the state's notice period.
Log any missing or late notice as an exception.
testing.done: termination notice delivery is verified for the sample with late or missing notices logged.

testing.step: Verify the for-cause report review and submission chain
actions: For each sampled for-cause termination, confirm General Counsel's review sign-off exists.
Confirm the state DOI submission confirmation exists and is dated within the required window.
Log any missing review or late submission as an exception.
testing.done: the for-cause review and submission chain is verified for the sample with gaps logged.

Log any post-termination bind as an exception.
Confirm exposure assessment was completed for any such bind.
testing.done: binding revocation is verified for the sample with any post-termination bind and its assessment logged.

testing.step: Trace remediation of prior out-of-window findings
actions: Pull tracker issues logged for out-of-window cases in the prior test period.
